items.title: An invertible module with trivial generic fibre over a flat family with integral fibres on a normal base is pulled back from the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a flat morphism with integral fibres from a locally Noetherian source onto a locally Noetherian integral normal base, an invertible module whose restriction to the generic fibre is trivial is the pullback of an invertible module on the base (statement lines 6967-6981). The counted proof is long and has three distinct layers: it produces a regular meromorphic section from a trivializing section of the generic fibre, defines the candidate module of meromorphic functions on the base and states the isomorphism claim, settles the affine case with a substantial symbolic-power computation over the normal base in which the product of the two ideals is shown to be principal so that both factors become invertible, and then glues over the target by comparing local generators along fibres, which is where the irreducibility of the fibres and the case hypothesis on the morphism are used to make the exceptional set closed (proof lines 6983-7090). It is H2: the argument is a complete author proof with real substance and the cited inputs are standard commutative algebra, but the author leaves 'some details omitted' in the glueing step, so no independent research-level claim is made.
